items.title: Fannie, MBA cut 2026 forecasts; plan for 6.8% rates
items.description: Economy Fannie, MBA cut 2026 forecasts; plan for 6.8% rates By Brad Finkelstein CloseText About Brad twitter nmnbrad mailto bradley.finkelstein@arizent.com linkedin brad-finkelstein-8b2b9a5/ Published September 21, 2026, 6:00 a.m. EDT | Updated September 21, 2026, 5:25 p.m. EDT 3 Min Read Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Email Both Fannie Mae and the Mortgage Bankers Association pushed down their respective mortgage finance forecasts for 2026 as rates continued their climb in September. Processing Content Much of this movement started even before indicators became strong that the Federal Open Market Committee would need to boost short-term rates, which it did on Sept. 16. While Keefe, Bruyette Woods' latest forecast calls for a 6.5% 30-year fixed rate mortgage based on a 4.75% 10-year Treasury by year-end, the two outlooks are similar on rate movements for the next six quarters (including this one), and call for 6.8% by year-end. Fannie Mae has rates at 6.7% for all of 2027; the MBA differs just in the first two quarters, calling for 6.8%. Compared to the August forecast , the MBA is 10 basis points higher from the current period through the second quarter next year. Fannie Mae is actually the same amount lower in the first two quarters of 2027. The MBA's projections were all baked in, to account for the Fed announcement and recent movements in the Treasuries, Joel Kan, deputy chief economist, said in an emailed statement. Most of Friday the 10-year Treasury was at 5%, the fourth day this week the yield was around this level. Fannie Mae put out its forecast on Sept. 15, while the MBA's is dated Sept. 16. For 2026, MBA's September forecast calls for a total of $2.123 trillion, with $1.423 trillion of this coming from purchase. A month ago, the total of $2.147 trillion included $1.434 trillion of purchase and $713 billion of refinance. It expects $2.101 trillion in 2027 and $2.16 trillion the following year. August's outlook for those years are $2.144 trillion and $2.184 trillion. Fannie Mae is pretty close to MBA in this year's prediction of $2.121 trillion; it sees $1.426 trillion of purchase volume. This is a reduction from the August outlook of $2.168 trillion , with $1.44 trillion from purchase and $728 billion of refinance. The government-sponsored enterprise going forward only has put out a 2027 forecast; September's edition called for $2.278 trillion, down from August's $2.294 trillion. BTIG analyst Douglas Harter commented on the Fannie Mae forecast in the Mortgage Finance Weekly report on Sept. 18, pointing out 30-year FRMs are pricing above 7% right now , higher than what the GSE called for. "In our opinion this introduces further downside risk to the forecasts next month," Harter wrote. BTIG's forecast, which cites MBA and Fannie Mae as inputs as well as its own data, calls for $1.42 trillion of purchase and $700 billion of refi activity this year. Next year, it expects $1.492 trillion and $670 billion, while for 2028 BTIG predicts $1.566 trillion and $750 billion respectively. This was unchanged from last week. Another reduction was in existing home sales. The MBA now forecasts approximately 4.105 million home sales on a seasonally adjusted annual rate; for August it projected 4.183 million. Fannie Mae now calls for 4.062 million in 2026, down from 4.106 million. "Demographics by themselves suggest it's really hard to see the number of existing home sales fall below 4 million," said Doug Duncan, an economics consultant and former chief economist at both Fannie Mae and the MBA. It is the fourth consecutive year of existing home sales running at about a 4 million pace, and this is the same as existing home sales back in 1995, and we have, give or take, 90 million more people than we had at that time, he pointed out. items.title: OHT Partners Breaks Ground on 360-Unit Multifamily Project in West Houston
items.description: HOUSTON — Austin-based developer OHT Partners has broken ground on Park Row, a 360-unit multifamily project in West Houston. The 14-acre site at 14192 Park Row Blvd. is located in the Energy Corridor, and the development will feature one- and two-bedroom units that will range in size from 702 to 1,257 square feet. Amenities will include a pool, clubhouse, fitness room, coworking space, communal kitchen, package lockers, a dog park, pickleball court and outdoor grilling and dining stations. Meeks + Partners is the project architect, and OHT’s in-house team is serving as the general contractor.

items.title: BREIT Lines Up $1.7B CMBS Loan For 19M SF Industrial Portfolio
items.description: BREIT Lines Up $1.7B CMBS Loan For 19M SF Industrial Portfolio September 21, 2026 | 4:42 pm ET Maddy McCarty, Houston Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust has secured a $1.71B CMBS loan to refinance a 76-property industrial portfolio, according to a Fitch Ratings report . Unsplash/Point3D Commercial Imaging Ltd. The world’s largest alternative asset management firm will collect a $105M dividend from the mortgage loan proceeds, which will also refinance $1.48B of existing debt and pay $40.6M in closing costs, Fitch's report states. Blackstone declined to comment on the loan. Fitch predicts the transaction will close Oct. 15. The floating-rate loan is expected to have an initial two-year term and three one-year extension options and require interest-only monthly payments, according to KBRA’s preliminary ratings report . The loan is being co-originated by Wells Fargo Bank , National Association, Goldman Sachs Bank USA, Bank of Montreal , Natixis Real Estate Capital and Societe Generale Financial Corp., per Fitch Ratings. It is secured by a warehouse and light industrial portfolio totaling 19M SF. The 76 properties in the portfolio are spread across 18 states, with 15 properties in Minnesota, six in Georgia, six in Texas and five in Tennessee. The largest property is a 935K SF warehouse and distribution facility in Quakertown, Pennsylvania. KBRA reported that the portfolio is 96% leased to 115 tenants. BREIT ’s full $104B portfolio of more than 4,500 properties is 90% concentrated in rental housing, industrial and data centers , according to BREIT’s second-quarter stockholder letter . Industrial properties make up 20% of the portfolio, second only to data centers, which account for 27%. The REIT officially exited the self-storage space by offloading its last 79 self-storage assets and spent $3.3B on data center development through its data center platform QTS during Q2. The disposition of its self-storage assets “reflects our broader strategy of actively managing BREIT’s portfolio and investing in our highest-conviction investment themes,” a Blackstone spokesperson said. BREIT’s industrial portfolio includes last-mile infill warehouses near dense population centers, which benefit from e-commerce demand, the Q2 report said. Blackstone said it expects artificial intelligence -driven purchases — which are expected to reach $1T by 2030 — to further drive e-commerce growth. Blackstone also saw data center-adjacent tenants account for 15% of new leases signed across its logistics platform in the last 18 months. items.title: Citadel Headquarters Project Under Stop-Work Order Following Rig Collapse
items.description: Citadel Headquarters Project Under Stop-Work Order Following Rig Collapse September 21, 2026 | 7:37 pm ET Chloe Gallivan, South Florida Construction on Citadel 's $2.5B Miami headquarters is on indefinite hold following an accident last week in which a drilling rig collapse sent four people to the hospital. Bisnow/Chloe Gallivan The stalled construction site for Citadel's headquarters following a rig collapse The accident is under investigation by federal and county safety officials, and the Miami-Dade County Department of Regulatory and Economic Resources has issued a stop-work order for the site, department spokesperson Tere Florin confirmed to Bisnow. The agency's Building and Environmental Permitting Division issued the order when the incident occurred the morning of Sept. 14 and "instructed the project contractor to submit a safety plan before the stop-work order is lifted," Florin wrote in an email. "Once the safety plan is submitted, it will be reviewed, and upon approval, the construction site may reopen." Related Cos. is developing the project on a site Citadel CEO Ken Griffin acquired in 2022 for $360M. Construction workers were in the process of deep soil mixing to ready the foundation for a massive skyscraper when a rig collapsed onto Brickell Bay Drive and crushed three cars and a Container Express box, trapping two construction workers inside. The driver of a white BMW that caught fire after it was crushed, along with two construction workers and the rig operator, were taken to the hospital with minor injuries. "Following an incident regarding one of our drill rigs, our concern is for the individuals affected, and we would like to thank the emergency services for their support," a representative for the project's contractor, Keller North America, said in a statement. "Our highest priority is the safety of our workers and the entire Brickell community, and we will work with the authorities and our project clients to conduct a full investigation." The Occupational Safety and Health Administration and Miami-Dade County's Consumer and Neighborhood Protection Division's unsafe structures team is investigating the Sept. 14 incident, the Miami Herald reported . It is unclear what caused the accident and how long the investigation will take. Until then, the site, which was supposed to begin vertical construction of one of the city's most anticipated office buildings by the end of this year, is in limbo. X/City of Miami Fire Rescue A drilling rig collapsed at the construction site of Citadel's future headquarters in Miami, injuring four people. A Citadel spokesperson directed inquiries to Related Cos ., which declined to comment. Ken Griffin is building a 1.7M SF office on the site at 1201 Brickell Bay Drive — roughly 560K SF of which will be occupied by his hedge fund, Citadel, and market maker, Citadel Securities. The billionaire spent four years and more than $770M to assemble a full city block in Brickell, which included buying out all of the condos in the 22-story Solaris building at 1155 Brickell Bay Drive, which is now blocked off and surrounded by fencing, aside from an entrance on the side. Project plans beyond the office building include a 300-unit residential tower and a parking garage, The Wall Street Journal reported , and possibly a hotel. The waterfront site has also been struggling with stormwater mitigation, which the developer has addressed by installing injection wells to divert stormwater back into the aquifer, but it still needs the permits to activate them, the WSJ reported. items.title: Eli Lilly Starts Building Record $6.5B Houston Manufacturing Facility
items.description: Eli Lilly Starts Building Record $6.5B Houston Manufacturing Facility September 21, 2026 | 5:06 pm ET Maddy McCarty, Houston Pharmaceutical giant Eli Lilly and Co. broke ground Monday on a Houston facility that will manufacture the company’s newly approved GLP-1 pill and other small-molecule medicines and advanced therapeutics. Eli Lilly and Co. Officials pose at the groundbreaking of Eli Lilly and Co.'s $6.5B biomanufacturing facility at Generation Park in Houston on Monday. Lilly broke ground on the $6.5B facility in Northeast Houston’s Generation Park about a year after announcing the planned investment . “This $6.5 billion Eli Lilly investment in Houston is the largest active pharmaceutical ingredient project in Texas history and will create more than 600 high-wage jobs, right here in Texas,” Gov. Greg Abbott said in a statement, adding that Texas is “the global hub for life sciences.” The company also announced Monday that it will provide $12.5M to support a relationship with nearby San Jacinto College to create a pathway into advanced chemical synthesis manufacturing careers. Bristol Myers Squibb , another pharmaceutical giant, announced in August that it would invest $2.3B to build a 600K SF manufacturing campus in Generation Park. These investments are big wins for McCord Development , the developer of the 4,300-acre master-planned Generation Park. McCord officials began laying the foundation to attract large-scale biotech and life sciences companies when it broke ground on Generation Park 13 years ago. They doubled down on life sciences-related education and workforce training initiatives after losing out on Amgen ’s $550M biomanufacturing project in 2021. Now Eli Lilly’s $12.5M investment in San Jacinto College will focus on developing training pathways and expanding infrastructure needed to produce technicians, operators, maintenance professionals and other manufacturing talent, the company said in its press release. Separately, Lilly is donating $2.5M to the San Jacinto College Foundation to support student scholarships. “This facility will run on the talent of this community, powered by our relationship with San Jacinto College,” Lilly Manufacturing Operations President Edgardo Hernandez said in the release. “We're hiring across the greater Houston area to help residents build careers close to home.” The Houston facility is Lilly’s fifth domestic active pharmaceutical ingredients production location announced since 2020 and part of the company’s $50B push to reshore medicine production . The facility will produce Foundayo, a synthetic oral GLP-1 medicine approved in the U.S. for weight management. The Food and Drug Administration approved the medicine on April 1 . Lilly is studying Foundayo for other uses, including Type 2 diabetes and obstructive sleep apnea, the company said. items.title: Paramount, Warner Bros. Settlement Preserves CRE Commitments For First 5 Years
items.description: Paramount, Warner Bros. Settlement Preserves CRE Commitments For First 5 Years September 21, 2026 | 4:27 pm ET Bianca Barragán, Southern California Wikimedia Commons/Coolcaesar The entrance to the Paramount lot along Melrose Avenue Paramount Skydance and the state attorneys general who sued to block its merger with Warner Bros. Discovery have agreed to a settlement , allowing the merger to proceed, The Wall Street Journal reported . The companies cannot sell their namesake studio lots in Los Angeles for the first five years after the deal, under the terms of the settlement. Additionally, the combined company must uphold any outstanding contracts it had to lease or develop studio facilities in any of the states involved within the first five years following the merger. The settlement does not require the combined company to stay in California, a possibility that Paramount CEO David Ellison had raised during the antitrust suit. Paramount relocating its headquarters and operations out of California could result in $1B to $2B in losses for the state in just the next five years, according to a report from the Los Angeles County Economic Development Corp. The antitrust lawsuit from a dozen states, led by California Attorney General Rob Bonta, would have gone to trial in March and could have delayed the merger until at least the middle of next year. The settlement removes the largest hurdle to the merger closing, as regulators in the U.S. and abroad have approved it, the WSJ reported. The terms of the settlement include a minimum theatrical release of 30 movies a year for the merged company and a requirement that the new company spends at least $1.5B on production in the U.S. in the five years after the merger closes, an amount representing a $300M increase over what the companies spent individually on production in 2025. “Today, we have secured a settlement that resolves our antitrust concerns of the Warner Bros./Paramount merger — concerns that the merger will lower output and increase prices — by guaranteeing massive investment in domestic film production and providing enforceable guardrails to help keep cable prices competitive,” Bonta said in a statement . But Bonta also underscored what the settlement didn’t do. “Let me be clear: This settlement is not a vote of support for this merger,” he added. The union of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery would bring a suite of TV networks, the CBS network and streaming services Paramount+ and HBO Max under one umbrella. It would also unite a portfolio of studio and office real estate, including millions of square feet of studio lots and leased office space. Warner Bros. owns a 2.6M SF film and television complex in Burbank, California, which holds 31 soundstages and 11 sets on the 110-acre main lot. Another Warner Bros. Burbank facility has 16 soundstages and is the television base for the 2028 Olympics . In the UK, Warner Bros. owns a 1.3M SF complex northwest of London with 350K SF of soundstages and a 100-acre back lot. Paramount Skydance owns the 1.2M SF Paramount lot on Melrose Avenue in Hollywood, a legendary property that includes roughly 30 soundstages. Globally, Paramount and its affiliated companies, including Viacom and CBS, occupy 8M SF. Its top landlords are Hudson Pacific Corp., Hackman Capital Partners, Kilroy Realty, Pimco Prime Real Estate, Goodman Group and Worthe Real Estate, according to CoStar News. Paramount also owns 2.1M SF across 14 properties, according to CoStar News . The delay to the Paramount/Warner Bros. merger began in July when the attorneys general filed an antitrust lawsuit to halt it, arguing that a merger of the media companies would harm competition between the two in a way that would negatively impact movie theaters, cable distributors and consumers. items.title: CUNY Buys Historic Bronx Post Office For $201M
items.description: CUNY Buys Historic Bronx Post Office For $201M September 21, 2026 | 8:15 pm ET Ciara Long, New York City A year after signing a long-term lease at the landmarked Bronx General Post Office for a new community college, the City University of New York has acquired the educational property. Google Maps The landmarked South Bronx Post Office at 558 Grand Concourse CUNY paid $200.9M for a commercial condo in the Concourse Village building, according to property records . The deal went under contract in March, according to PincusCo, which first reported the deal, and closed Sept. 10. Prolific Bronx developer Maddd Equities acquired the 175K SF building at 558 Grand Concourse Ave. last July for $44M and struck a deal to lease it to the city's university system a few months later. CUNY announced last September that it signed a 35-year lease at the building for a Hostos Community College outpost, expanding on the community college’s specialized nursing, radiology, dental hygiene and other education programs. When it first signed with Maddd Equities, CUNY agreed to pay roughly $550M in rent over the lease's duration. The deal also gave the system the option to buy the property outright within the first five years of its lease, according to The City Reporter . Hostos graduated roughly 2,500 science, technology, engineering, mathematics and health students in 2025 but expects to be able to double that number by converting the former post office, CUNY Chancellor Felix Matos Rodriguez said at the time . An entity associated with Maddd Equities agreed to carry out around $70M worth of renovations on the building at the time the lease was signed, with the city government pitching in $12.3M. CUNY acquired the entire four-story building, except for a segment of the basement and ground floors, which was split into a separate commercial condominium unit, according to a document filed with the city in July. The 1937-built property hadn’t operated as a post office since 2012. Its exterior was landmarked in 1975, and a portion of its interior was landmarked in 2013. Youngwoo Associates bought the Bronx General Post Office in 2014 for $19M, then partnered with investor Bristol Group and spent approximately $60M on the project in the hopes of redeveloping the building with a food hall, retail and office space. But Youngwoo put the property back on the market for $75M in 2024, and Maddd Equities acquired it a year later, borrowing $31M from an entity linked to LibreMax Capital for the acquisition. items.title: WareSpace Expands Microbay Flex Industrial Concept With South San Francisco Acquisition
items.description: WareSpace Expands Microbay Flex Industrial Concept With South San Francisco Acquisition September 21, 2026 | 7:50 pm ET Rob Sabo, San Francisco Bay Area Courtesy of WareSpace WareSpace is transforming a 64K SF industrial building in South San Francisco into 86 microbay flex suites ranging from 200 SF to 2K SF. As some functionally obsolete, low-slung industrial buildings in the San Francisco Peninsula are being targeted for demolition to make way for new multifamily towers, one developer is zeroing in on those same assets to create dozens of new small-bay flex industrial warehouses. Washington, D.C.-based WareSpace beefed up its portfolio of 34 industrial assets spanning more than 3.2M SF with the acquisition of 161 Starlite St . in South San Francisco. WareSpace plans to renovate the 1965-built, single-story industrial property into 86 move-in-ready microbay flex spaces ranging from 200 SF to 2K SF. WareSpace paid just over $16M for the property and will spend a few million more renovating and subdividing the building, co-founder and CEO Joseph Ely told Bisnow . It is the first acquisition in the Bay Area for WareSpace, which has stood up its model of flex industrial spaces in major metros such as Austin, Atlanta, Houston, Seattle and Chicago. “The Bay Area has a great small-business presence, but like a lot of other major cities, it has had a dwindling supply of small spaces,” Ely said. “They are being taken offline or are at capacity when more small businesses are being created or growing.” Rising rents and tightening vacancy rates for all types of commercial real estate in cities up and down the Peninsula have developers targeting obsolete office and industrial buildings for a wave of new mid-rise multifamily projects . Industrial vacancy for the Peninsula was 5.6% in the second quarter , according to CBRE . At 15.1M SF of inventory, South San Francisco accounts for nearly half of the Peninsula’s 35.1M SF of industrial space. Small industrial spaces, however, are virtually nonexistent. A LoopNet search of spaces 2K SF or smaller yielded just two available options in South San Francisco. That dearth of small-bay space creates opportunity for WareSpace to reposition the property and deploy its business model of rolling shared racking, loading docks, utilities, WiFi, security, trash and cleaning into a flat monthly bill. This model simplifies move-in and operations for small contractors, service firms, distributors, e-commerce companies and other small enterprises, Ely said. WareSpace leases are inked on six- or 12-month terms, and tenants can shrink or grow their footprint at any time, he added. “The LoopNet search tells the whole story,” he said. “There are no options for [small] businesses. We try to make it a one-stop shop, and they can rightsize at any time to adapt to their current business realities.” WareSpace is able to repurpose much of the building’s existing infrastructure, including restrooms, office space, and loading and drive-in docks, Ely said. Once the existing four tenants in the building move out, the warehouse space will be gutted and developed into private microbay flex suites. WareSpace is working through development plans and will let the project go to bid once building plans are approved and permits are secured. The property is expected to come online in Q2 2027, although that target could shift, Ely said. “The actual space build-out is pretty quick, but there are a lot of compliance and zoning requirements that you have to go through,” he said. “This market in particular has seen a lot of transaction activity around the AI boom, with businesses and companies buying their own buildings or trying to upgrade power. Building departments are inundated with plans and permits right now.” Continue reading this story with a free account Log in or register Contact Rob Sabo at rob.sabo@bisnow.com Related Topics: Joseph Ely , Warespace

items.title: Walker & Dunlop Arranges $86M Refi for Flushing Affordable Quartet
items.description: New York & Tri-State CRE News In Your Inbox. Sign up for Connect emails to stay informed with CRE stories that are 150 words or less. New York Tri-State + Outer Boroughs + Apartments | September 21, 2026 By: Paul Bubny Walker Dunlop Arranges $86M Refi for Flushing Affordable Quartet Walker Dunlop arranged an $86,443,000 Freddie Mac refinancing of a 506-unit multifamily portfolio in the Flushing neighborhood of Queens. The loan was originated on behalf of Iris Holdings Group, a national affordable housing preservation and investment firm, and refinances the portfolio’s existing debt while supporting its long-term affordability. The Flushing Preservation Portfolio is comprised of four elevator buildings at 44-15, 45-15 and 45-35 Colden St. and 137-20 45th Ave. The 481,000-square-foot portfolio features covered parking, views of Kissena Corridor Park and features a mix of studio, one-bedroom, two-bedroom and three-bedroom units. Iris Holdings Group partnered with the New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development in 2024 to preserve this project at varying levels of affordability for the next 40 years. Walker Dunlop Affordable Housing Debt and Capital Markets Real Estate Finance, led by John Gilmore and Harvey Pava, arranged the fixed-rate financing. If you’re reading about the multifamily industry, you should be in the room with its leaders. Connect Apartments brings together the executives featured in Connect CRE’s coverage for an afternoon of high-level insights and unmatched networking on September 22 at The Biltmore in LA . items.title: Flexible Lab Provider Closing 84K SF Boston Location
items.description: Flexible Lab Provider Closing 84K SF Boston Location September 21, 2026 | 5:19 pm ET Jon Banister, East Coast Editor The lab space provider that occupies the same complex as the Boston Bruins' practice facility appears to be skating on thin ice. Google Maps The 40 Guest St. building that SmartLabs occupied at Boston Landing SmartLabs is ending operations at its 84K SF space at 40 Guest St. in the Boston Landing development in Brighton , the Boston Business Journal reports . The flexible lab space facility had some remaining tenants that are now searching for new space, according to BBJ. The 40 Guest St. building also served as SmartLabs' headquarters. NB Development Group , the real estate arm of New Balance , owns the building. The Boston Landing complex features the shoemakers' headquarters as well as practice facilities for the Bruins and Celtics. SmartLabs and NB Development didn't respond to Bisnow' s requests for comment. The closure is the latest in a series of setbacks for SmartLabs, a coworking-style lab space operator founded in 2015. After growing quickly during the pandemic-era life sciences boom, the company began shrinking its footprint and facing legal issues after the industry's sharp downturn started in 2023. In 2024, SmartLabs closed its two Bay Area locations as part of a pullback from the West Coast. In September 2025, BioMed Realty sued SmartLabs for "repeatedly" failing to pay rent at its 21 Erie St. location in Cambridge. The operator no longer lists that space on its website, and its entity tied to that location filed for bankruptcy in November, BBJ reported. SmartLabs also terminated a 140K SF lease it had signed at the CambridgeSide development late last year. The only remaining Boston-area location listed on SmartLabs' website is at 301 Binney St. in Kendall Square . Greater Boston's lab market continues to struggle, with vacancy rates above 30%, but some signs of demand growth have emerged this year. Massachusetts-based companies raised $3.45B in venture capital in the first half of this year, up 25% year-over-year, according to MassBio . In July, JLL reported that the number of life sciences tenants looking for space in the region had increased from 28 in the first quarter to 49 in the second.
